issues.legal_issue: A pending suit for injunction may be amended before trial to seek declaration of title and recovery of possession when the amendment changes the relief but does not alter the suit’s basic structure.
material_facts: The plaintiff had filed a suit seeking a permanent injunction concerning agricultural land, and the defendant disputed the plaintiff’s possession.
Before trial, the plaintiff sought to amend the plaint, alleging that the defendant had dispossessed him during the suit and seeking declaration of title and recovery of possession.
The court found that the amendment did not alter the basic structure of the suit, would help determine the real controversy, and could avoid a separate suit and multiplicity of proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The amendment should be allowed, subject to payment of costs and protection against depriving the defendant of any prescriptive rights that may have accrued.
issues.legal_principle: Order VI Rule 17 CPC empowers a court to permit amendments needed to determine the real questions in controversy. As stated in Mst. Rukhmabai v. Lala Laxminarayan, AIR 1960 335, a suit should not automatically be dismissed for omission of an appropriate relief where the plaintiff seeks to amend. Pre-trial amendments are generally allowed more liberally because the opposing party has an opportunity to meet the amended case; delay alone is not a ground for refusal. The court considers prejudice in the circumstances of the particular case.

rule.if: pending_suit_amendment and amendment_before_trial and basic_structure_unchanged and relief_changes_only and amendment_resolves_real_controversy and amendment_avoids_separate_proceeding

predicates.pending_suit_amendment: A party sought to amend pleadings in a civil suit that was still pending.
predicates.amendment_before_trial: The amendment was sought before the trial commenced.
predicates.basic_structure_unchanged: The proposed amendment left the basic structure of the existing suit unchanged.
predicates.relief_changes_only: The proposed amendment changed the relief sought without changing the suit’s basic structure.
predicates.amendment_resolves_real_controversy: The proposed amendment would assist in determining the real questions in controversy between the parties.
predicates.amendment_avoids_separate_proceeding: Allowing the proposed amendment would avoid the need for a separate proceeding and reduce multiplicity of proceedings.

issues.definition: When a party seeks a pre-trial amendment in a pending suit that preserves the suit’s basic structure, changes only the relief, helps determine the real controversy, and avoids a separate proceeding, the amendment is permitted.

issues.legal_issue: A court may direct that amended relief does not relate back to the date of the original suit when relation back could defeat a prescriptive right alleged to have accrued before the amendment application.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought the new reliefs about eleven years after filing the original suit, alleging that dispossession occurred during the suit.
The defendant contended that he had perfected title by adverse possession and that relating the new reliefs back to the original filing date would deprive him of the benefit of elapsed time.

The court allowed the amendment but directed that the new reliefs be treated as sought on the date the amendment application was filed, without deciding whether the defendant had in fact acquired title by adverse possession.
issues.conclusion: The reliefs of declaration of title and recovery of possession are deemed to have been sought on the date the amendment application was filed, rather than the date of the original suit.
issues.legal_principle: An amendment ordinarily relates back to the date of the suit, but that doctrine is not universally applicable. A court may direct that an amendment take effect from the date of the amendment application. The court relied on Siddalingamma v. Mamtha Shenoy, [2001] 8 SCC 561, and applied this discretion to protect a defendant’s alleged prescriptive rights from being defeated by relation back.

predicates.pending_suit_amendment: A party sought to amend pleadings in a civil suit that was still pending.
predicates.added_relief_sought_after_substantial_de: The party sought new relief after a substantial period had elapsed since filing the original suit.
predicates.defendant_claims_prescriptive_right_accr: The opposing party claimed that a prescriptive right accrued during the period before the amendment application.
predicates.relation_back_could_defeat_claimed_right: Treating the new relief as sought from the original filing date could deprive the opposing party of the benefit of the claimed prescriptive right.

issues.definition: When new relief is sought after substantial delay in a pending suit, the opposing party claims a prescriptive right accrued during that delay, and relation back could defeat that claim, the new relief takes effect from the amendment application.
